Since \(p\nmid D\) and \(w_i\mid D\), every nonzero exponent \(D/w_i\) is prime to \(p\).  The partial derivatives have no common zero on the punctured affine cone, so \(X\) is quasi-smooth.

Consider
\[
\pi\colon\mathbb{P}^n\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbf{w},
\qquad [y_0:\dots:y_n]\longmapsto[y_0^{w_0}:\dots:y_n^{w_n}].
\]
It is finite and surjective and carries the smooth Fermat hypersurface
\[
F=\Bigl\{\textstyle\sum_i c_i y_i^D=0\Bigr\}\subset\mathbb{P}^n
\]
onto \(X\).  After base change to \(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q\), the fibers are the orbits of the finite abelian group \(G=(\prod_i\mu_{w_i})/\mu_d\), where \(d=\gcd(w_0,\ldots,w_n)\) and \(\mu_d\) is embedded diagonally; its order is prime to \(p\), and \(X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q}=F_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q}/G\).  If \(\pi:F\to X\) denotes the quotient map, then \(\pi\) is finite, \((\pi_*\mathbb{Q}_\ell)^G=\mathbb{Q}_\ell\), and taking \(G\)-invariants is exact.  Therefore
\[
H^*_c(X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q},\mathbb{Q}_\ell)
\simeq H^*_c(F_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q},\mathbb{Q}_\ell)^G.
\]
The cohomology of \(F\) is pure and satisfies Poincar\'e duality.  The pairing restricted to the invariant subspaces is nondegenerate: if an invariant class pairs nontrivially with some class, averaging the latter over \(G\) preserves that pairing.  Thus the invariant cohomology is pure and self-dual, and so is \(X\).  The same argument applies verbatim to every nonempty sector.  For the arithmetic of diagonal hypersurfaces in the unweighted case see \cite{gouvea-yui}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- exa-9: body_md -->
For \(X=\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbf{w}\) the sector \(X^{(e)}\) is \(\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf{w}_e}\), of dimension \(\#\{i:e\mid w_i\}-1\), which equals \(n\) exactly when \(e\) divides every \(w_i\). So the sectors are equidimensional if and only if each \(e\in E_\mathbf{w}\) divides all of the \(w_i\), that is, if and only if the prime-to-\(p\) parts of \(w_0,\dots,w_n\) are all equal. This is precisely the criterion of \cite[Thm.~7.6]{paper-1}, recovered here from the geometry of the sectors.
<!-- end exa-9 -->
<!-- exa-10: body_md -->
\label{exa:fe-fail}
Let \(p\neq 2,3\) and \(X=\{x_0x_2+x_1^3+x_0^3=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}(1,1,2)\), of weighted degree \(3\). Its partial derivatives are \(x_2+3x_0^2\), \(3x_1^2\), \(x_0\), which vanish simultaneously only at the origin, so \(X\) is quasi-smooth; it is a rational curve, and it passes through the \(\mu_2\)-point \([0:0:1]\). Here \(E_\mathbf{w}=\{1,2\}\), \(X^{(1)}=X\) has \(q^r+1\) points, and \(X^{(2)}=X\cap\{x_0=x_1=0\}=\{[0:0:1]\}\) is a single point, of dimension \(0\neq 1\). With \(o_2=1\),
\[
Z^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak X,t)=Z(X,t)\,Z(X^{(2)},t)=\frac{1}{(1-t)^2(1-qt)},
\]
which admits no functional equation under \(t\mapsto1/(qt)\), while \(Z(X,t)=1/((1-t)(1-qt))\) does. The number of twists is therefore \(q^r+2\) for every \(r\), compared with \(q^r+1\) coarse points.
<!-- end exa-10 -->
<!-- exa-11: body_md -->
\label{exa:fe-diag}
Let \(p\) be odd and \(X=\{x_0^4+x_1^4+x_2^2+x_3^2=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}(1,1,2,2)\), a weighted diagonal surface of degree \(4\); it is quasi-smooth since the exponents \(4,4,2,2\) are prime to \(p\). Then \(E_\mathbf{w}=\{1,2\}\) and \(X^{(2)}=\{x_0=x_1=0,\ x_2^2+x_3^2=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}(2,2)\) consists of two points, rational over \(\mathbb{F}_{q^{r}}\) precisely when \(q^r\equiv1\pmod 4\), so \(o_2=1\) and \(\delta_2=0\neq2\). Accordingly
\[
\#\pi_0(\mathfrak X(\mathbb{F}_{q^{r}}))=|X(\mathbb{F}_{q^{r}})|+\bigl|X^{(2)}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{r}})\bigr|,
\]
and the second term equals \(2\) when \(-1\) is a square in \(\mathbb{F}_{q^{r}}\), and \(0\) otherwise.  The sector dimensions are \(2\) and \(0\), so the product has no functional equation centered at dimension \(2\), although each sector is self-dual.
<!-- end exa-11 -->
<!-- rem-17: body_md -->
\label{rem:fe-necessity}
The purity hypothesis in \cref{cor:fe-exact} is used only to exclude cancellation of the extreme poles by odd-degree cohomology.  Geometric irreducibility ensures that each nonempty sector contributes exactly one \(H^0\) class and one top class before the multiplicity coming from the Jordan-totient exponent.  Without these hypotheses a more refined criterion would have to keep track of Frobenius orbits of components and possible cancellations; we do not claim such a criterion here.
<!-- end rem-17 -->
<!-- rem-18: body_md -->
The constants implicit in (iv) are those of the Lang--Weil estimate for \(X\) and for the components of \(\Sigma_r\), and are controlled by the \(\ell\)-adic Betti numbers of these varieties through the trace formula. When \(p\nmid w_i\), these are the Betti numbers of the stack \(\mathfrak X\) and of its twisted sectors \cite{Behrend}.
<!-- end rem-18 -->
